IX-C1.name: Noetherian formal series, complete quotients and henselian finite algebras
IX-C1.statement_used: Finite formal power series over a Noetherian ring are Noetherian; quotients of a complete Noetherian local ring remain complete; a finite algebra over a henselian local ring is a finite product of local rings, so a finite domain is local.
IX-C1.matching: Used on the actual IsCO rings, the finite eigenvalue algebra C[b], and complete prime quotients. Integrality makes the origin evaluation land in O; uniqueness of the maximal ideal proves localness before reducing quotient labels. Successive approximation arguments are given directly.

IX-C2.name: Proper projective flag varieties and the valuative criterion
IX-C2.statement_used: A locally projective morphism is proper; a quasi-compact morphism is universally closed exactly when it satisfies the existence part of the valuative criterion.
IX-C2.source: Stacks Project, Lemma29.44.5 tag01WC and Proposition26.20.6 tag01KF.
IX-C2.matching: The symplectic flag variety is explicitly a closed incidence/isotropy subvariety of a product of Grassmannians. The schematic closure of the actual generic flag is proper and surjects the integral base. A chosen K-point then extends over the given valuation ring. This does not assume smoothness, flatness or uniqueness of flags.

IX-C3.name: Weak Nullstellensatz
IX-C3.statement_used: Every nonzero finite-type algebra over an algebraically closed field has a rational closed point.
IX-C3.matching: Applied only to the nonzero finite-type invariant fibre. Nonzero follows from the weight-zero retraction before field extension. Full formal evaluation is justified separately using positive valuations and finite monomial decompositions.

IX-C4.name: Finite extensions of complete discrete valuation fields
IX-C4.statement_used: A finite separable extension of a complete discretely valued field has a unique extended valuation, is complete, and has finite valuation ring with finite residue field if the original residue field is finite.
IX-C4.source: J.S.Milne, Algebraic Number Theory, v3.08, Theorems7.38--7.40; Stacks tag09E8.
IX-C4.matching: Captures finitely many algebraic flag-basis entries in a single complete DVR inside the original V. Equal-characteristic purely inseparable extensions are handled separately by adjoining ell-power roots of a uniformizer over the perfect finite residue field; Milne is not misquoted as already proving that part.

IX-C5.name: Minkowski: no nontrivial everywhere-finite-unramified extension of Q
IX-C5.statement_used: A finite extension of Q unramified at every finite prime is Q.
IX-C5.source: J.S.Milne, Algebraic Number Theory, v3.08, Theorem4.9, printedp72/PDFpage74.
IX-C5.matching: Applied to each finite continuous reduction of a powered character. The character is first shown trivial on every original inertia group, including ell. Separatedness is used only after these finite assertions. No assertion about arbitrary infinite unramified extensions is used.

IX-C6.name: Density theorem over an algebraically closed field
IX-C6.statement_used: The image of an algebra in the endomorphisms of a finite-dimensional simple module over an algebraically closed field is the full endomorphism algebra.
IX-C6.source: P.Etingof et al., Introduction to Representation Theory, January10,2011, Theorem2.5(i), p24; Section2.5 finite-dimensional algebra proof.
IX-C6.matching: Used only to turn simplicity on G_L back into the literal matrix-span Irr predicate. The finite-index semisimplicity, self-twist construction, injective characteristic-zero transport and distinct residual-character contradiction are proved in IX10.
